2609.28784.title: Script Choice in LLMs: Evidence for Late-Layer Commitment
2609.28784.paper_summary: In this paper, we investigate how script knowledge is distributed across the layers of LLMs using two complementary interpretability methods: logistic regression probing and logit-lens analysis. Our probing experiments reveal a clear asymmetry: both the input script and the instructed output script are encoded in the earliest layers of the network, while, in contrast, commitment to the actual output script emerges only in the final layers, with the model's intermediate representations defaulting to Latin throughout most of the layers. This two-stage process is confirmed by logit-lens analyses, which show that script commitment consistently occurs at the very last layers of the LLMs. Together with the weaker script-following performance observed in smaller models, these results form a converging body of evidence linking script commitment to model depth, with broader implications for the design of sufficiently deep, inclusive multilingual architectures.
2609.28784.paper_summary_zh: 在本文中，我們研究了如何通過兩種互補的可解釋性方法：邏輯回歸探測和邏輯透鏡分析，來分析腳本知識在大型語言模型（LLMs）層中的分佈。我們的探測實驗揭示了一個明顯的非對稱性：輸入腳本和指令輸出的腳本都在網絡的最早層中被編碼，而與此相對，對實際輸出腳本的承諾僅在最後幾層中出現，模型的中間表示在大多數層中默認為拉丁文。這一兩階段過程得到了邏輯透鏡分析的確認，該分析顯示腳本承諾始終發生在LLMs的最後幾層中。再加上在較小模型中觀察到的較弱的腳本跟隨性能，這些結果形成了一個趨同的證據體，將腳本承諾與模型深度聯繫起來，對設計足夠深且包容的多語言架構具有更廣泛的啟示。
